It really started around the time I lost a major solar contract and the financial pressure started getting really tight.\n\nDoctor: Besides losing interest, have you also been feeling down, hopeless, or depressed most days during this time?\n\nPatient: Yes, pretty much every day I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest, like something terrible has happened even when nothing has. It just hangs over me from my first cup of coffee until I crawl back into bed at night.\n\nDoctor: Have you also noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration during this time?\n\nPatient: Yes, I'm struggling with all of those. I lie awake for hours worrying about bills and then wake up at 3 or 4 AM unable to sleep, and I have to force myself to eat because food tastes like cardboard. My concentration is also shot—I have to reread simple emails several times and get completely frozen by basic decisions.\n\nDoctor: Did these symptoms start within a few months of the contract loss and financial stress, and do they feel mainly tied to that situation? Or do they seem to have continued even when the stress is not on your mind?\n\nPatient: Yes, they started just a couple of months after I lost that big contract and the financial pressure hit. But now, it's become constant—even when I'm not actively thinking about the bills or the business, that heavy feeling is just there all day long.\n\nDoctor: Have these symptoms made it hard for you to work, manage daily responsibilities, or take care of yourself, and do you ever have thoughts that life is not worth living or that you'd be better off dead?\n\nPatient: Yes, it’s severely impacted everything—I’m missing bid deadlines, turning in reports late, and letting bills pile up while my income drops and I just isolate myself at home. On the really bad nights, I do catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or even picturing crashing my truck on the highway, though I don't have any actual plans to do anything.\n\nDoctor: Before the contract loss, had you ever had a similar period of depressed mood or loss of interest lasting at least two weeks, or is this the first time it has happened?\n\nPatient: No, this is the first time I've ever experienced anything like this. Even when nothing new has gone wrong or when I'm just trying to relax on my days off, that heavy feeling and lack of interest are there every single day. It just doesn't lift, even if the financial pressure isn't actively on my mind.\n\nDoctor: Have your symptoms improved at all as the financial and work stress has eased, or have they stayed just as severe even during periods when things were going better?\n\nPatient: Honestly, the financial and work stress hasn't actually eased up or gotten better at all over this past year. The pressure has been completely constant, so there haven't really been any \"better\" periods, and my symptoms have stayed just as heavy and severe the entire time.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any period of at least a couple of weeks during this past year when your mood and interest improved noticeably, or have the symptoms been present nearly every day without relief?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't had any break or improvement at all. But since then, it has evolved into something much deeper and more persistent than just a normal reaction to stress. It feels like a heavy, constant depression that has completely taken over my life for over a year now.\n\nDoctor: Did your symptoms begin only after the contract loss and financial stress, and do they feel mainly tied to that stressor rather than coming on for no clear reason?\n\nPatient: Yes, they definitely started only after I lost that big solar contract and the financial pressure began.
